Every number on this site can be rebuilt from these files, and all of them
are free to download.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {csvPlain, json, count, pct, megabytes, fileSize, longDate, emptyNote, guard, h, REPO_URL, DATA_URL, DATA_RAW_URL, RELEASES_URL} from "./lib.js"
// Tables only: no chart library on this page (d3 and Plot are never loaded).
import {table} from "./charts.js"
ch = ({table})
raw = json("data/manifest/raw.json")
files = csvPlain("data/files.csv")
dictionary = json("data/datapackage.json")
reports = json("data/reports/index.json")
// A button that copies a value, and says so to screen readers.
copyButton = (text, label) => {
  const b = h("button", {type: "button", class: "copy", "aria-label": label}, "Copy");
  b.addEventListener("click", async () => {
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      b.textContent = "Copied";
    } catch (e) {
      b.textContent = "Press Ctrl+C";
    }
    setTimeout(() => { b.textContent = "Copy"; }, 2000);
  });
  return b;
}
```

## Start here

The daily figures are small tables you can open in a spreadsheet. Each link
opens the latest version of the file; your browser may show it as plain
text, and you can save it from there.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<ul class="download-list">
  <li><a href="${DATA_RAW_URL}/ontime/daily.csv"><code>ontime/daily.csv</code></a> has the share of departures on time, one row per day.</li>
  <li><a href="${DATA_RAW_URL}/ontime/routes.csv"><code>ontime/routes.csv</code></a> has the same figures for each route on each day.</li>
  <li><a href="${DATA_RAW_URL}/quality/daily.csv"><code>quality/daily.csv</code></a> has the daily grades of the tracking feed.</li>
  <li><a href="${DATA_RAW_URL}/files.csv"><code>files.csv</code></a> lists every larger file with its address and its SHA-256, a fingerprint for checking a download.</li>
  <li><a href="${DATA_RAW_URL}/datapackage.json"><code>datapackage.json</code></a> describes every table and column in a form a program can read.</li>
</ul>`
```

::: {.link-row}
[All the larger files (Releases)](https://github.com/dfladagermccullugh-bot/Open-Island-Transit-Data/releases)
[Browse the data branch](https://github.com/dfladagermccullugh-bot/Open-Island-Transit-Data/tree/data)
[License](https://github.com/dfladagermccullugh-bot/Open-Island-Transit-Data/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md)
:::

Every timestamp in the files is in UTC. A service day is a calendar date in
Pacific time, and hours of the day are Pacific too. Shares are fractions
from 0 to 1. The [codebook](codebook.qmd) explains every file and every
column.

## What's in the archive

The larger tables have one file for each service day and live in monthly
Releases on GitHub: the raw archive in `raw-YYYY-MM` and everything parsed
from it in `parsed-YYYY-MM`.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const tables = [...(dictionary?.dailyTables ?? []), ...(dictionary?.resources ?? [])];
  if (tables.length === 0) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The list of tables");
  const where = t => t.path
    ? h("a", {href: `${DATA_RAW_URL}/${t.path}`}, h("code", {}, t.path))
    : h("code", {}, `${t.release}/${t.pathPattern}`);
  return ch.table(tables.map(t => ({...t, columns: t.schema?.fields?.length ?? null})), {
    caption: "Every table in the archive", wide: true, pageSize: 40,
    columns: [
      {key: "title", label: "Table", sortable: false},
      {key: "oneRowIs", label: "One row is", sortable: false},
      {key: "columns", label: "Columns", align: "right", format: count, sortable: false},
      {key: "format", label: "Format", format: v => v === "parquet" ? "Parquet" : "CSV", sortable: false},
      {key: "name", label: "Where", format: (v, t) => where(t), sortable: false},
    ],
  });
}, "The list of tables")
```

## Files for one day

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// The days that have files, newest first, for the picker.
viewof fileDay = {
  const days = [...new Set(files.map(f => f.service_date instanceof Date ? f.service_date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : String(f.service_date ?? "")))].filter(Boolean).sort().reverse();
  const select = h("select", {id: "file-day"}, ...days.map(d => h("option", {value: d}, longDate(d))));
  const picker = h("div", {class: "route-picker"}, h("label", {for: "file-day"}, "Service day"), select);
  if (days.length === 0) picker.hidden = true;
  Object.defineProperty(picker, "value", {get: () => select.value || null});
  return picker;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (files.length === 0) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The list of files");
  const iso = d => d instanceof Date ? d.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : String(d);
  const rows = files.filter(f => iso(f.service_date) === fileDay);
  return ch.table(rows, {
    caption: `Files for ${longDate(fileDay)}`, wide: true, pageSize: 40,
    columns: [
      {key: "name", label: "File", format: (v, f) => h("a", {href: f.url}, h("code", {}, v))},
      {key: "table", label: "Table"},
      {key: "bytes", label: "Size", align: "right", format: v => fileSize(v)},
      {key: "sha256", label: "SHA-256", sortable: false,
       format: v => h("span", {class: "hash"}, h("span", {title: v}, `${String(v).slice(0, 12)}…`), copyButton(String(v), "Copy the full SHA-256"))},
    ],
  });
}, "The list of files")
```

To check a download, compute its SHA-256 and compare it with the one listed
here or in `files.csv`. On macOS and Linux that is
`shasum -a 256 <file>` or `sha256sum <file>`. Once a month is complete, its
Release also holds a `SHA256SUMS` file that `sha256sum -c` can check in one
step.

## Archived days

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const rows = Object.values(raw?.days ?? {}).map(d => ({
    day: d.service_date, fetches: d.fetch_rows, ok: d.ok_rows,
    bytes: (d.files ?? []).reduce((a, f) => a + (f.bytes ?? 0), 0),
    release: d.release_tag}));
  if (rows.length === 0) return emptyNote("unavailable", "The list of archived days");
  return ch.table(rows, {
    caption: "Archived service days", sort: {key: "day", descending: true}, pageSize: 20,
    columns: [
      {key: "day", label: "Service day", format: v => longDate(v)},
      {key: "fetches", label: "Fetch attempts", align: "right", format: count},
      {key: "ok", label: "Successful", align: "right", format: count},
      {key: "bytes", label: "Size of the raw archive", align: "right", format: v => megabytes(v)},
      {key: "release", label: "Release", format: t => t ? h("a", {href: `${RELEASES_URL}/tag/${t}`}, t) : "not yet uploaded"},
    ],
  });
}, "The list of archived days")
```

## Monthly reports

Once a month is over, we write up a summary of it and add a checksum
verification file to its downloads, so you can confirm that your copies
match ours exactly.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const rows = Array.isArray(reports) ? reports : [];
  if (rows.length === 0) return h("p", {class: "empty"}, "No month is complete yet.");
  // The count of missing days was named days_missing at first.
  const missing = r => r.days_missing_count ?? (Array.isArray(r.days_missing) ? r.days_missing.length : r.days_missing);
  return ch.table(rows.map(r => ({...r, missing: missing(r)})), {
    caption: "Monthly reports", sort: {key: "month", descending: true}, wide: true,
    columns: [
      {key: "month", label: "Month", format: m => h("a", {href: `${DATA_URL}/reports/${m}.md`}, m)},
      {key: "days_archived", label: "Days archived", align: "right", format: count},
      {key: "missing", label: "Days missing", align: "right", format: count},
      {key: "vehicle_uptime", label: "Collector uptime", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 2)},
      {key: "trip_coverage", label: "Trip coverage", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
      {key: "timepoint_observed_share", label: "Timepoint events observed", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
      {key: "on_time_share_of_observed", label: "On time (of observed)", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
      {key: "bytes", label: "Size", align: "right", format: v => megabytes(v)},
    ],
  });
}, "The list of monthly reports")
```

## Using and citing the data

When we started collecting, Island Transit's feeds carried no published
license or terms of use. Our [license file](https://github.com/dfladagermccullugh-bot/Open-Island-Transit-Data/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md)
explains how we share the archived data. If you use the data or the figures,
please credit them as "Open Island Transit Data, derived from Island
Transit's public GTFS feeds," with the date you downloaded them. The
repository's [citation file](https://github.com/dfladagermccullugh-bot/Open-Island-Transit-Data/blob/main/CITATION.cff)
has the same information in a form reference managers can read.
